question: What is the term for a push or pull that can move an object or change its shape?
explanation: A force is simply a push or pull acting on an object or tissue. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it helpful for midwives to understand physical forces on the body?

options.A: To prevent back strain and injuries while caring for patients
options.B: To calculate the exact speed of a baby in the birth canal
options.C: To measure the chemical makeup of muscles during lifting
options.D: To determine the precise room temperature needed for labor

explanation: Knowing how body forces work helps midwives use proper posture and movements to protect themselves from physical strain. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h1)

question: What two key features define a vector in body mechanics?
explanation: A vector is defined by having both a numerical size (magnitude) and a direction. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h2)

question: In a force diagram, what does the length of an arrow usually show?

options.B: The temperature of the contracting muscle
options.C: The distance traveled by a joint
options.D: The age of the person moving

explanation: Longer arrows represent stronger forces acting in that direction. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the term for the physical stress placed on bones and joints during everyday tasks?
explanation: Musculoskeletal loading refers to the physical forces and stress placed on the skeletal and muscular systems. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h3)

question: If you twist your spine while lifting something heavy, what type of stress does this put on your spinal discs?
explanation: Twisting introduces angled forces that create harmful shear and bend stresses on the spine. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h3)

question: When a single muscle force is split into perpendicular parts, what are those parts called?
explanation: Forces acting at angles can be separated into vector components to study their individual effects. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main job of the rotatory component of a muscle force?

options.A: To cause movement or rotation around a joint
options.B: To increase the body temperature of the patient
options.C: To push joint bones out of place
options.D: To cool down muscle fibers during exercise

explanation: The rotatory component acts across the bone to create movement at the joint. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which body part usually acts as the fulcrum in human lever systems?
explanation: Joints serve as the pivot points, or fulcrums, that bones rotate around. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why does holding a heavy object close to your chest reduce strain?

options.A: It shortens the distance from the pivot, lowering the rotational force
options.B: It increases how fast blood pumps to the arms
options.C: It stops gravity from acting on the human body
options.D: It turns the bone into a rigid, unmoving structure

explanation: Keeping the load closer to the joint reduces the torque your muscles must fight against. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these actions should you avoid when lifting a heavy object at work?

options.A: Twisting your torso while holding the load
options.B: Bending at your knees and hips
options.C: Keeping your feet apart for stability
options.D: Keeping the load close to your body

explanation: Twisting while lifting puts dangerous shear stress on the spine and should always be avoided. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h6)

question: How should a midwife position her body to stay stable while helping a mother move from a bed to a chair?

options.A: With her heels lifted high off the floor
options.B: With a wide base of support and feet apart
options.D: With her knees locked completely straight

explanation: A wide base of support improves stability and helps manage physical loads safely during patient transfers. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T1#BMP112_U2_T1_h6)
